title: Non-symmetry of biconstrained two-step reachability
author: Alec Kriebel
abstract: The biconstrained reachability function ψ(x, y) is the largest fraction of the first part that some vertex of the third part must reach in two steps, over all finite tripartite graphs satisfying minimum-degree conditions in both directions on each adjacent pair. We answer its symmetry question negatively: |ψ(13/27, 14/27) − ψ(14/27, 13/27)| ≥ 1/108. The proof establishes the exact rational-boundary formula ψ(1 − θ, θ) = 1 − θ/d(θ), where d(θ) is a minimum integer degree of a positive rational regular incidence template. An existing seven-type example and its complement bound both relevant integers by four, making equality impossible. Neither exact value nor their ordering is needed or asserted.
short_summary: Swapping two minimum-degree thresholds changes the best guaranteed two-step reachability, with an explicit gap of at least 1/108.
plain_language_draft: Imagine three groups of vertices, with connections only between neighboring groups. Each adjacent pair must satisfy minimum connection requirements in both directions. How large a fraction of the first group must some vertex in the third group reach in two steps? The paper claims that exchanging the two connection thresholds can change this universal guarantee. At thresholds 13/27 and 14/27, the two guarantees differ by at least 1/108. The argument does not determine which guarantee is larger.
exact_result_draft: For the biconstrained function ψ defined over finite simple tripartite graphs, |ψ(13/27,14/27) − ψ(14/27,13/27)| ≥ 1/108. More generally, for every rational θ in (0,1), ψ(1−θ,θ) = 1−θ/d(θ), attained by a finite graph. Here d(θ) is the minimum unweighted maximum row degree among finite binary templates with distinct columns and strictly positive rational probability weights b,q satisfying Mq=θ1 and Mᵀb=θ1.
interesting_result: An exact formula on the rational boundary converts a universal extremal-graph question into an integer invariant. The inherited seven-type template and its complement bound the two relevant integers by four, which forces a quantitative asymmetry without evaluating either integer.
attribution_draft: Paul Seymour posed the biconstrained symmetry question in Oberwolfach Reports 1/2019. Chudnovsky, Hompe, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl developed the finite weighted-graph framework and supplied the seven-type template in their 2022 paper Concatenating Bipartite Graphs. This note’s claimed contribution is the rational-boundary formula and its deduction of an explicit asymmetry gap. The predecessor’s symmetry theorem concerns the related one-direction function φ; its Theorem 12.2 treats only the minimal-value case for ψ.
limits_draft: The result concerns a universal guarantee over finite graphs, rather than the directional reachability of one chosen graph. All four minimum-degree inequalities matter; reached vertices are counted once, regardless of how many paths reach them. The formula is stated for rational θ in (0,1). The note does not evaluate the two invariant minima, the exact pair of ψ-values, their ordering, irrational-boundary values, or the full function away from this boundary. The two explicit graphs supply upper bounds only.
